findings.summary: The reviewed runtime and current model contracts distinguish verified management evidence from unprobed Internet availability, withdraw current business claims when evidence is unavailable, and keep proved interface/default-route dependency ahead of concurrent resource pressure. The independently replayed verdict truth contract passed 10/10.

Canonical query routing, real search/filter/sort behavior, object history and typed inspectors are backed by model state rather than placeholder DOM. Structural route maturity replay passed with 0 complete, 18 bounded-readonly, 0 fallback and 1 unavailable route; the section-model evidence contract also passed missing, zero, historical and unavailable cases, so this review does not relabel bounded routes as complete modules.

OverviewPanel and OperationalSectionPage select one mobile or desktop renderer branch instead of mounting parallel presentation trees. The bound report confirms one non-nested main landmark across Overview, desktop domains, connection and contract-error states, and its 619/620 capacity check reports no duplicate task DOM.

The independently replayed architecture gate passed its source budgets (mobile 240, domain 420, evidence 516) with a 12 px minimum mobile text floor. A direct scan of 28 source CSS files found zero !important declarations and zero font-size declarations below 12 px.

Focused replay passed backend security, HTTPS explicit-risk handling, SSH pinning, bounded sessions, password-free profile storage, API schema, collector transport, response headers, read-only runtime labeling, canonical URL/offline signaling, TypeScript checking, verdict truth, section models, route structure and mobile semantic contracts. No P0 or P1 engineering/security defect was reproduced within the reviewed local scope.

For the reviewed artifact, frameworkAssetIdentity records an exact 153-file SHA-256 input match at digest 61cb234390ac23b4f2fc9055ac1571e44bd6011f190290fdb77293542bfde0a8. A fresh replay against the later mutable worktree does not match its current manifest (manifest 0225480bed6dcbafb080cab89dccefd9bf02e2e0cad3cda4a513273565f1723e versus source 1a303d8348b40369ac1ffe854ff3d6b68d520f1c5e030c7c7d7cb7fe3021cefd); that post-artifact drift is outside this historical binding and prevents using this record as evidence for current source or release readiness.

This engineering-architecture review is bound only to the named Step910 production-runtime artifact, whose 271 checks and 146 screenshot records pass while worktreeClean=false and releaseEvidenceEligible=false. The artifact quarantine/identity contract independently classifies it as historical-or-worktree evidence and disallows it as current release input; no clean-SHA, deployment or public-release approval is claimed.
